newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA-SAS, MAERSK INTERESTED IN STATE AIRLINE.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA-SAS, MAERSK INTERESTED IN STATE AIRLINE.

text.p: Scandinavian airline SAS and Denmark's Maersk Air have expressed an interest in taking part in the privatisation of Lithuanian Airlines, Lithuanian European Affairs Minister Laima Andrikiene said on Thursday.
"SAS have been interested but Maersk has been more interested," Andrikiene told Reuters in an interview.

Lithuanian Airlines is one of the key companies on the government's privatisation list and Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius has said that the government wants to sell more than 50 percent of the national carrier.
SAS has already bought a stake in Latvia's national airline, Air Baltic, while Maersk, owned by Danish industrial giant A.P. Moeller, owns a controlling share in Estonian Air.

Andrikiene said that mainly Scandinavian airlines were interested in the Lithuanian carrier and that more general international interest was greater in other state companies such as the telecoms firm.
